content:
thought
The test image shows a whole sugarcane plant with significant yellowing of the leaves and a bushy, grass-like appearance due to numerous thin tillers. The leaves appear narrow and pale yellow/chlorotic. This strongly suggests the 'whole_plant' part is affected.

I will now read the `part_index.md` file to confirm the affected plant part and narrow down the possible classes.

thought
The reference image for Grassy_Shoot (LeafNet_136.jpg) shows a whole plant with a very bushy, grass-like appearance and significant yellowing of the leaves. This is a very strong match for the test image.

Now I will view the reference image for Yellow_Leaf to compare.

thought
The reference image for Yellow_Leaf shows a single dried, yellowed leaf. While the test image has yellowing leaves, the overall presentation of the Yellow_Leaf reference (a single, completely dried leaf) does not match the bushy, grass-like appearance of the whole plant in the test image. The "Grassy_Shoot" reference image was a much better match.

I will now view the reference image for Pokkah_Boeng (leaf) as per my plan.

thought
The reference image for Pokkah_Boeng (LeafNet_15.jpg) shows a leaf with malformations, twisting, and some damage. This does not match the bushy, yellowing, grass-like appearance of the test image.

Next, I will view the reference image for Sett_Rot (stem).

thought
The reference image for Sett_Rot (LeafNet_10.jpg) shows dried, somewhat discolored lower leaves and what appears to be part of the stem near the soil. This image does not show the characteristic "bushy, grass-like appearance" or extensive tillering seen in the test image.

So far, Grassy_Shoot is the best match. I will continue with the rest of the plan to use all 8 reference image views. Next is Brown_Spot (leaf).

thought
The reference image for Brown_Spot shows a single leaf with a distinct reddish-brown spot. This does not match the widespread yellowing and bushy appearance of the test image.

I will continue viewing the reference images as per the plan. Next is Leaf_Scald (leaf).

thought
The reference image for Leaf_Scald shows a leaf with a prominent white "pencil line" and some yellowing/streaking. This is clearly different from the overall bushy, yellowed plant in the test image.

I will continue viewing reference images. Next is Streak_Mosaic_Scsmv (leaf).
